tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Which Meerko workspace (brand) this connection acts on now. Every other tool works in that workspace.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the user's Meerko workspaces, one per brand, with the one this connection acts on marked `current`. Workspaces share one plan and credit balance; tables, mailboxes, sequences and replies are per workspace.

tools.name: switch_workspace
tools.description:
Point this connection at another of the user's workspaces (ids from list_workspaces). Every later call, in this conversation and any other using this connection, acts on that brand: its leads, mailboxes and sequences.
Switch only when the user names the brand, and say which workspace is now active.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create a workspace for another brand. It shares the user's plan and credits, starts empty, and isn't switched to: call switch_workspace to work in it.

tools.name: rename_workspace
tools.description: Rename a workspace. Only its owner can.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List all prospect tables in the Meerko workspace, with their columns and row counts.

tools.name: create_table
tools.description: Create a new prospect table (e.g. 'Fintech CTOs Spain'). Columns are optional; they are also auto-created on import.

tools.name: add_column
tools.description:
Add a column to a table. Give it a `prompt` to make it an AI column: an instruction that you (the agent) answer per row, e.g. "Score ICP fit 1-5 for {{company}}: {{description}}" or "Write a one-line opener for {{first_name}} at {{company}}".
Meerko doesn't run the prompt itself. Fill the column with get_pending_cells + update_rows. Calling this again with a new prompt replaces the instruction.

prompt.description: Instruction for an AI column; {{column_key}} inserts that row's value

tools.name: get_pending_cells
tools.description:
Fetch rows whose AI column is still empty, each with the column's instruction already filled in from that row ("instruction") plus the full row data.
Answer each instruction yourself from the row data (and research, if the instruction asks for it), then save all answers in one update_rows call. Repeat while "remaining" > 0.
Write "N/A" when a row lacks what the instruction needs, so it isn't returned again.

column.description: The AI column's name or key

tools.name: update_rows
tools.description: Write values into existing rows by row id. Each update's `data` is merged into the row; new keys become new columns. Max 1,000 rows per call.

tools.name: import_rows
tools.description: Insert rows (objects of column -> value) into a table. Keys are normalized to snake_case and unknown keys become new columns. Max 10,000 rows per call.

tools.name: query_rows
tools.description: Read rows from a table, each with its pipeline stage. `filter` is an exact-match object on column keys, e.g. {"country": "Spain"}; `stage` filters by stage (new, contacted, replied, meeting, won, lost).

tools.name: find_people
tools.description:
Search the lead database for people and save them as rows in a table (first_name, last_name, title, company, domain, company_size, industry, location, linkedin_url, company_linkedin_url).
Filters are objects keyed by field. Text fields take {include?: string[], exclude?: string[]}; numeric fields take range operators {">=": n, "<=": n}.
Use alpha-2 country codes for location ("ES", "US"). Expand titles across languages and acronyms (["CTO", "Chief Technology Officer", "Director de Tecnología"]).
People fields: currentJobTitle, pastJobTitle, firstname, lastname, location, keyword, skills, languages, school, currentCompanyName, currentCompanyWebsite, currentCompanyUrn, "currentCompany.industry", "currentCompany.location", "currentCompany.keyword"; ranges: "currentCompany.headcount", "currentCompany.revenue", totalYearsOfExperience; growth: "currentCompany.headcountGrowth" {timespan: "6months"|"12months"|"24months", min, max}.

limit.description: Max results to fetch (default 25). Each result costs 1 credit (none with your own Icypeas key); count first.

table_name.description: Name for a new table, used when table_id is omitted

count_only.description: Only return how many leads match. Free; use before a paid search.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description:
Search the lead database for companies and save them as rows in a table (company, domain, industry, employees, location, founded_year, description, linkedin_url, company_urn).
Filters are objects keyed by field. Text fields take {include?: string[], exclude?: string[]}; numeric fields take range operators {">=": n, "<=": n}.
Use alpha-2 country codes for location ("ES", "US"). Expand titles across languages and acronyms (["CTO", "Chief Technology Officer", "Director de Tecnología"]).
Company fields: name, industry (LinkedIn industry names, e.g. "Financial Services", "Software Development"), location, keyword, domain, type; ranges: headcount, revenue (USD); growth: headcountGrowth {timespan, min, max}.
To get decision-makers at the found companies, pass their company_urn values to find_people as currentCompanyUrn.

limit.description: Max results to fetch (default 25). Each result costs 1 credit (none with your own Icypeas key); count first.

table_name.description: Name for a new table, used when table_id is omitted

count_only.description: Only return how many leads match. Free; use before a paid search.

tools.name: enrich_rows
tools.description:
Find work emails (from first_name, last_name and domain or company columns) and verify them, writing email, email_certainty and email_verification back to each row.
Only rows missing a result are processed, at most `limit` per call (~3s per row). Keep calling while `remaining` > 0.
Costs: 8 credits per email found, 1 per verification; misses are free. Emails found as ultra_sure/very_sure count as verified at no cost.
email_certainty values: ultra_sure, very_sure, probable (deliverability unconfirmed), not_found, missing_input (row lacks a name or domain).

filter.description: Only enrich rows matching this exact-match filter

overwrite.description: Re-run rows that already have a result

tools.name: connect_gmail
tools.description: Start connecting an inbox to send from: Gmail/Google Workspace, Outlook/Microsoft 365, Zoho, Fastmail or any IMAP/SMTP provider. For Outlook pass provider "outlook": it returns a Microsoft sign-in link for the user to open and approve. For the others the user connects it themselves with an app password: give them the returned link (or CLI command) and its steps. Then call list_mailboxes to confirm it's connected. Never ask for a password in chat.

provider.description: outlook for Outlook / Microsoft 365; gmail (default) or other for the rest

email.description: Account to pre-select on Microsoft's or Google's sign-in page

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: List connected sending mailboxes with their daily limit, what they may send today (effectiveLimit, lower while a new mailbox ramps up; rampDay) and status. A mailbox in `error` status lost access and must be reconnected with connect_gmail.

tools.name: update_mailbox
tools.description:
Set a mailbox's daily send limit, the sender name recipients see, or its ramp.
New mailboxes ramp up automatically: they start at 10 emails a day and grow to their daily limit over 21 days (list_mailboxes shows effectiveLimit and rampDay). Turn the ramp off only for an inbox that already sends regularly.

ramp.description: true restarts the 21-day ramp from today; false sends at the full daily limit now

tools.name: check_domains
tools.description: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC for every domain the workspace sends from. A missing record is a common reason mail lands in spam: tell the user which record to add before starting a sequence. "managed" means consumer Gmail, where Google handles it. DKIM is checked at Google Workspace's default selector ("google").

tools.name: send_test_email
tools.description: Send a test email from a connected mailbox to check it works. Only send to the user's own address.

tools.name: create_sequence
tools.description:
Create a DRAFT email sequence for a table, sent from a pool of one or more connected mailboxes (see list_mailboxes). Each lead is assigned one mailbox and every step comes from it, in the same thread; more mailboxes means more volume per day.
Write short, plain, personal emails: step 1 with a subject, 1-3 follow-ups that reply in the same thread. Use only {{vars}} that the table's rows actually have; rows missing a used variable are skipped at enrollment.
Then: preview_sequence to check, enroll_rows, show the user the preview and enrollment counts, and only call start_sequence after the user approves.

assignment.description: How leads are spread over the mailboxes: capacity (default) gives more to mailboxes that can send more today; even gives each the same number

subject.description: Only for step 1; follow-ups reply in the same thread

body.description: Plain text. Use {{column_key}} for row values, e.g. {{first_name}}. An unsubscribe line is appended automatically.

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the recipients, e.g. Europe/Madrid (default)

window_start_hour.description: Local hour sending starts on weekdays (default 9)

tools.name: update_sequence
tools.description: Edit a sequence's name, mailbox pool, assignment, send window or steps (steps replace all existing ones; pause an active sequence first). Changing mailbox_ids moves leads not yet emailed to the new pool; leads already mid-thread stay on their mailbox, or stop if it was removed.

subject.description: Only for step 1; follow-ups reply in the same thread

body.description: Plain text. Use {{column_key}} for row values, e.g. {{first_name}}. An unsubscribe line is appended automatically.

tools.name: preview_sequence
tools.description: Render every step of a sequence for one row (the first row by default), exactly as it will be sent, plus any template variables that row is missing.

tools.name: enroll_rows
tools.description: Enroll rows from the sequence's table. Skips (and counts) rows with no email, an undeliverable email, an unsubscribed address, a missing template variable, or already enrolled. Enrolling doesn't send anything until the sequence is started.

tools.name: start_sequence
tools.description: Start sending a sequence. Real emails go to real people from the user's mailbox: only call this after the user has seen the preview and explicitly approved. Sends respect the send window, the mailbox's daily limit and spacing.

tools.name: pause_sequence
tools.description: Pause a sequence; nothing more is sent until it's started again.

tools.name: list_sequences
tools.description: List sequences with status and enrollment counts.

tools.name: sequence_stats
tools.description: A sequence's enrollment states (active, completed, replied, unsubscribed, failed...), emails sent, reply rate, and its mailbox pool: each mailbox's sends today against its limit, ramp day and number of leads.

tools.name: list_replies
tools.description:
Replies to the user's sequences that nobody has classified yet (newest first). Each has the reply text (quoted history removed), the earlier emails in the thread, and the prospect's table row.
Meerko already stopped the sequence for anyone who replied, and handled bounces, unsubscribe requests and out-of-office replies by itself (hidden here unless include_automatic).
Read each reply, decide its intent and save it with classify_reply. Summarize the interested ones and questions for the user.

intent.description: Only replies with this intent (then classified ones are included)

tools.name: classify_reply
tools.description: Set a reply's intent after reading it: interested (wants to talk / asks for a meeting), question (asks something before deciding), not_now (timing), not_interested, referral (points to someone else), wrong_person, other. Set handled: true when no further action is needed.

tools.name: draft_reply
tools.description:
Save a draft answer to a reply (from list_replies). Nothing is sent: the user reviews it first.
Write like a person answering an email: short, specific to what they said, in their language, with one clear next step (e.g. two meeting times or a booking link if the user gave you one). Sign off with the sender's first name: Gmail doesn't add the user's signature to emails sent through Meerko. Drafting again for the same reply replaces the pending draft.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description: Pending drafts with the reply each answers, the thread so far and the prospect's row. Show them to the user for approval.

tools.name: approve_draft
tools.description: Send a draft as a reply in the same email thread, from the user's mailbox. Only call this after the user has read this specific draft and explicitly said to send it. Pass `body` if the user edited the text.

tools.name: discard_draft
tools.description: Throw a pending draft away.

tools.name: pipeline
tools.description: Lead counts per stage (new → contacted → replied → meeting → won → lost), for one table or the whole workspace. Meerko moves leads to contacted when the first email is sent and to replied when they answer; meeting, won and lost are set with move_stage.

tools.name: move_stage
tools.description: Move leads (rows) to a pipeline stage, e.g. meeting when a call is booked, won or lost. Use query_rows with `stage` to find leads at a stage.

tools.name: delete_rows
tools.description: Permanently delete leads (rows) from a table, e.g. poor fits or a person who asked to be removed. Their sequences stop; emails already sent and do-not-email entries (unsubscribes, bounces) are kept. Prefer move_stage to `lost` to keep a lead's history. Confirm with the user before deleting.

tools.name: delete_table
tools.description: Permanently delete a table with all its rows and its paused or draft sequences. Refused while one of its sequences is active (pause it first). Confirm with the user before deleting.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Show the workspace's credit balance (null when self-hosted with your own provider keys, or when credits are off). Searches and email finding stop when it runs out; sending and replies keep working. If it's low, tell the user so before a large search.

prompts.name: find-leads
prompts.title: Find leads
prompts.description: Build a lead list from your ideal customer, with verified emails.

arguments.name: icp
arguments.description: Who you sell to, e.g. 'heads of growth at Series A fintechs in Spain'

prompts.name: write-sequence
prompts.title: Write a sequence
prompts.description: Draft a 3-step email sequence for a table, in your voice.

arguments.name: offer
arguments.description: What you're offering, if it isn't obvious

prompts.name: triage-replies
prompts.title: Triage replies
prompts.description: Sort new replies by intent and draft answers for you to approve.

prompts.name: pipeline
prompts.title: Pipeline
prompts.description: See who's interested, booked and won, and what needs you.
